consequential_difficulty_tests.difficulty: Does debitum dimisit denote true forgiveness, and does the final judgment undo the gift-first argument?
witnesses: Chrysostom, Matthew Homily 61, sections 1–5 (NPNF I.10 retained text)
Augustine, Sermon 83/NPNF Sermon XXXIII, sections 1–8 (NPNF I.6 retained text)
Aquinas, Summa theologiae III q88 aa1–3, https://www.newadvent.org/summa/4088.htm
consequential_difficulty_tests.outcome: Survives substantively: the pardon is real; new mercilessness exposes ingratitude and incurs judgment. Chrysostom says the until does not promise eventual repayment. Augustine joins forgiveness to real correction. Aquinas provides a later technical distinction about renewed punishment, which the research does not attribute retroactively to the Fathers. Aquinas source retention/seal remains RES-001.

consequential_difficulty_tests.difficulty: Does the Collect promise immunity from the bodily suffering narrated in the Offertory?
witnesses: Augustine, Psalm 89/NPNF 90 sections 1–4 and Psalm 118/NPNF 119 Caph 81–88
consequential_difficulty_tests.outcome: Survives substantively: Gregory separates malicious will from permitted power, antecedent guilt from the purpose of Job’s trial, and bodily affliction from divine custody. Augustine preserves ongoing temptation and final expectation. Chrysostom expressly develops Paschal food and an unfinished journey after Exodus. The Mass-wide connection is identified as editorial. Gregory source retention/seal remains RES-001.
